raw_text:
Below is the full 12-week program summary for your 30‑year‑old advanced lifter at 20 weeks pregnant (OB cleared for moderate strength). It integrates strength, higher-intensity Phase 2, pressing work (no supine), pregnancy-safe core, cardio, and the nutrition guidance you requested earlier. It follows your contraindications (no supine after week 16, no maximal attempts, no contact sports) and uses symptom-guided autoregulation. Use RPE and symptoms > heart-rate zones (pregnancy alters HR). If any red-flag symptoms occur (bleeding, painful contractions, sudden fluid loss, dizziness/fainting, chest pain, calf pain/swelling, decreased fetal movement), stop and contact OB.

How to read this plan
- Frequency: 3 gym strength sessions/week (A, B, C), 3 cardio sessions/week (2 steady-state + 1 interval), plus 1 optional recovery session (walk/pool/yoga). Core is integrated 2 short sessions/week + optional recovery core day.
- Session length: Strength sessions ~45–60 min; cardio 20–40 min depending on type.
- Intensity guidance: Phase 1 RPE ~6–7; Phase 2 RPE ~7–8 for main lifts (submax only); Phase 3 RPE ~6–7. Avoid true maximal attempts (no 1RM testing).
- Positioning: No flat supine exercises. Replace flat bench with incline bench (30–45°), seated machine presses, or landmine presses. All core avoids supine crunches; focus on anti-rotation/anti-extension.
- Progression: Conservative overload — increase 2–5% when top reps achieved for 2 sessions and no symptoms. Use RPE autoregulation.
- Breathing: Diaphragmatic inhale, gentle brace, exhale on concentric; avoid Valsalva.

Summary by phase
Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Adaptation & baseline. Higher rep work, technique, core and breathing integration. RPE 6–7.
Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Strength emphasis and higher intensity (she wants to feel like training). Lower reps, heavier submax loads on main lifts (RPE 7–8). Increased unilateral and carry work. Cardio includes one higher submax interval session per week.
Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12: Maintenance & transition. Preserve strength, prioritize recovery, prepare for postpartum. Week 12 peak session: heavy-but-submax single/double at RPE 7–8; do NOT test true 1RM.

Weekly structure (throughout)
- Mon: Strength Session A + short cardio warm-up (10–15 min) + Core Session 1
- Tue: Cardio steady-state 25–40 min (walk/pool/bike) or active recovery
- Wed: Strength Session B + Core Session 2
- Thu: Cardio interval session (submax intervals, 20–30 min total) or pool work
- Fri: Strength Session C + optional short cardio or sled pushes
- Sat: Active recovery / prenatal yoga / light walk or optional core mobility
- Sun: Rest

Detailed week-by-week plan

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4 (Establish technique, breathing, core basics)
Weeks 1–4 common notes:
- RPE 6–7 for main work.
- Rest 90–150s between main compound sets; 60–90s for accessories.
- Core Session 1 and 2 integrated after Strength A and Strength B respectively.

Week 1 (example; repeat similar structure Weeks 2–4 with gradual increases)
Session A (Lower bias)
- Warm-up: 5–7 min bike + mobility + bar/DB warm sets
- Safety-bar goblet or safety-bar squat — 4 x 8
- Seated single-arm dumbbell row — 4 x 8 each
- Romanian deadlift (DB or trap bar) — 3 x 8
- Standing Pallof press — 3 x 10 each side
- Farmer carry (DBs) — 3 x 40–60 m
Core Session 1 (~10 min)
- Tall-kneeling diaphragmatic breathing + TVA draw 3 x 8 breaths
- Bird-dog 3 x 8 each side
- Pallof press (band) 3 x 8 each side
- Side-lying trunk lifts 2 x 10 each

Session B (Upper bias)
- Warm-up
- Incline dumbbell press (30–45°) or seated machine chest press — 4 x 8
- Lat pulldown or single-arm lat pulldown — 3 x 8–10
- Seated DB overhead press — 3 x 8 each
- Hip thrust alternative (standing cable pull-through) — 3 x 8
- Seated kettlebell carry or suitcase carry — 3 x 30–45s
Core Session 2 (~10 min)
- Quadruped breathing + pelvic tilt 3 x 8 breaths
- Modified side plank (knees down) 3 x 20–30s each
- Standing cable anti-rotation chops 2 x 8 each

Session C (Mixed)
- Warm-up
- Trap-bar deadlift — 4 x 6–8
- Split squat or Bulgarian split squat — 4 x 8 each (back foot elevated optional)
- Cable face pulls + band external rotation superset — 3 x 12
- Single-leg RDL — 3 x 8 each
- Glute bridge on wall/standing hip abduction — 3 x 12
Core finisher (afterwork)
- Side plank progression 3 x 20–30s each side
Cardio (Week 1)
- 2 steady-state walks/bike sessions 25–30 min (RPE 5–6)
- 1 short interval session (bike or pool) 10–12 min work total: 30s hard/90s easy x 6–8 (RPE ≤7)

Weeks 2–4:
- Slightly increase loads if comfortable (~2–5% when reps achieved). Maintain RPE and symptoms monitoring. Progress core hold times moderately and increase carry distances. Cardio volume stable.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8 (Higher intensity — she wants to feel like training)
Key adjustments
- Main lifts move to heavier, lower-rep schemes (e.g., 5 x 4–6, 4 x 4–5, 5 x 3–4) at RPE 7–8. No maximal attempts.
- Increase unilateral work (heavy Bulgarian split squats, single-leg RDLs) and loaded carries.
- Cardio: one interval session with submax intervals (RPE 7–8 short efforts) + 2 steady state sessions.
- Increase core intensity: stronger Pallof resistance, longer/heavier carries, tall-kneeling anti-extension holds.

Week 5 (example)
Session A (Lower heavy)
- Warm-up
- Safety-bar box squat — 5 x 4–6 @ RPE 7–8
- Trap-bar deadlift — 4 x 4–6 @ RPE 7
- Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 6 each leg @ RPE 7–8
- Tall-kneeling cable anti-extension — 3 x 10
- Farmer carry heavy — 3 x 50–60 m
Core Session 1
- Tall-kneeling breathing + TVA 2 sets x 8 breaths
- Bird-dog with 2–3s pause 3 x 10 each
- Pallof press cable 4 x 8–10 each side

Session B (Upper heavy — pressing focus)
- Warm-up
- Incline barbell or heavy incline DB press — 5 x 4–6 @ RPE 7–8 (safety pins/spotter)
- Seated chest-supported row — 4 x 6–8
- Seated DB overhead press — 4 x 6
- Landmine single-arm press — 3 x 8 each
- Face pulls 3 x 12–15
Core Session 2
- Quadruped anti-extension (dead-bug style) 3 x 8 each
- Side plank progressions 3 x 25–40s each
- Single-arm overhead carry 3 x 30–45s each side

Session C (Posterior/unilateral heavy)
- Warm-up
- Trap-bar deadlift heavier variant — 5 x 3–5 @ RPE 7–8
- Single-leg RDL heavy — 4 x 6 each @ RPE 7
- Incline chest press (lighter) superset with single-arm row — 3 x 8 each
- Cable pull-throughs — 3 x 10–12
- Prowler sled pushes 5 x 25 m (RPE 7)
Core finisher
- Pallof 3 x 10 each side; modified incline plank 3 x 20–30s
Cardio (Phase 2)
- 2 steady-state 30–40 min sessions (RPE 5–6)
- 1 interval session: e.g., bike 6–8 x 30s @ RPE 7–8 / 90–120s easy, total interval work 10–15 min
Progression rules
- Increase load 2–5% when top reps performed for two consecutive sessions at target RPE and no symptoms. Use RPE autoregulation; back off if RPE >8.5 or any symptoms.

Weeks 6–7 (intensity ramp)
- Week 6: Increase loads slightly on main lifts as tolerated. Continue pressing heavy incline 5 x 4 or 5 x 5 at RPE 7–8. Increase carry weights/distances.
- Week 7: Peak Phase 2 intensity but still submax. Example main set schemes: box squat 6 x 3–4 @ RPE 8; trap bar 4 x 3–4 @ RPE 8; incline press 5 x 4 @ RPE 8. Keep accessory volume moderate.
- Week 8: Slight reduction in overall volume (deload-ish week) but maintain challenging loads (RPE 7). Reduce accessory sets by 1–2 sets.

Phase 3 — Weeks 9–12 (Maintenance & transition; week 12 peak session is submax)
Goals
- Maintain or slightly increase strength depending on recovery.
- Prioritize movement quality, pelvic-floor prep for postpartum, and adequate recovery.
- Week 12 “peak” session: heavy-but-submax singles/doubles up to RPE 8 only. No true 1RM testing.

Weeks 9–11 (sample)
Session A
- Box squat (safety-bar) 4 x 5–6 @ RPE 7
- Seated chest-supported row 4 x 8
- Trap-bar RDL 3 x 6–8
- Pallof 3 x 12 each
- Farmer carry 3 x 50 m
Core: bird-dog, tall-kneeling TVA work

Session B (press-focused)
- Incline DB press 4 x 5–6 @ RPE 7
- Seated DB overhead press 3 x 6–8
- Single-arm landmine press 3 x 8 each
- Face pulls 3 x 15
Core: side plank, cable chops

Session C
- Trap-bar deadlift 4 x 4–5 @ RPE 7
- Step-ups or reverse lunges 3 x 8 each
- Incline press 3 x 6–8 lighter
- Cable pull-throughs or standing hip extension 3 x 10
- Carries 3 x 40–50 m
Core: Pallof presses, modified plank holds

Cardio (Phase 3)
- 2 steady-state 25–35 min (lower if fatigue)
- 1 interval session with reduced volume/intensity (short intervals at RPE ≤7)
- Swap to more pool work/walking if pelvic/back discomfort increases

Week 12 — Peak week (safe peak session; NO 1RM)
- Objective: let her feel heavy work and record submax performance without maximal attempts. Use RPE-based singles/doubles and submax rep-max conversions to estimate progress.
- Structure (example peak session):
  - Warm-up thoroughly (10–12 min bike + mobility + ramp sets).
  - Movement 1 (Incline barbell press): Work up to 1–2 heavy singles or doubles at RPE 7–8 — stop there. Record weight and RPE.
  - Movement 2 (Trap-bar deadlift): Work up to 1–2 heavy singles/doubles at RPE 7–8 — stop. Record weight and RPE.
  - Movement 3 (Safety-bar box squat or heavy step-ups): 3 x 3–5 at RPE 7
  - Core: Pallof 3 x 10 each side + single-arm carry 2 x 40 m
  - Cool-down and breathing drills.
- Do NOT attempt to test a true 1RM while pregnant. If she wants an objective number, estimate 1RM via submax sets and equations — do not chase it physically.

Nutrition & recovery (summary)
- Energy: maintenance +200–400 kcal/day (commonly +300 kcal in 2nd trimester), adjust by weight gain, appetite, and OB guidance.
- Protein: 1.2–1.8 g/kg/day — target 1.6–1.8 g/kg for lean-mass preservation for an advanced lifter if tolerated. Distribute evenly across 3–4 meals + snacks.
- Carbs: remaining calories; ensure a minimum ~175 g/day per general pregnancy guidelines; increase around training days +25–50 g pre/post-workout in Phase 2.
- Fat: 25–35% of calories with emphasis on unsaturated fats and DHA (200–300 mg/day).
- Continue prenatal vitamin; ensure adequate iron, vitamin D, calcium, iodine, choline; consult OB for labs and supplement adjustments.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day minimum; more with exercise/heat; include electrolytes if heavy sweating or lightheadedness.
- Sleep: prioritize 7–9 hours; add naps if needed. Two rest days/week recommended.
- Pelvic floor: daily gentle activation/awareness; avoid forceful bearing-down; refer to pelvic-floor physio for any incontinence or heaviness.

Cardio summary (integrated)
- Frequency: 3/week (2 steady-state, 1 interval), optional recovery session.
- Intensity: RPE 5–7 mostly; in Phase 2 allow RPE 7–8 for short interval work only (no maximal sprints).
- Modalities: walking (incline), recumbent/upright bike, elliptical, pool/aqua, rowing at moderate intensity, sled pushes.
- Avoid overheating, breath-holding, and sustained high HR — use talk test.

Core summary (integrated)
- 2 short core sessions/week post strength + optional pool/core day.
- Exercises: tall-kneeling breathing + TVA, bird-dog, Pallof press, side plank variations, single-leg RDL (stability emphasis), carries, modified incline plank.
- Avoid supine crunches/sit-ups and heavy loaded flexion; regress on coning/doming or pelvic-floor symptoms.

Safety, monitoring, and autoregulation
- Stop and consult OB for bleeding, painful contractions, sudden fluid loss, chest pain, severe dizziness, calf swelling or pain, or decreased fetal movement.
- If any set causes dizziness, lightheadedness, excessive breathlessness, or pelvic heaviness/leakage, reduce intensity, reduce sets, and refer to pelvic-floor physio if needed.
- Use RPE autoregulation; if RPE drifts >1 point higher than target across sessions, reduce load or volume.
- Progress conservatively: +2–5% when top reps achieved across two sessions and symptoms absent.
